source.title: A comparative study of transformer-based embeddings for topic coherence
source.authors: Alex Ding; Tarun Rapaka; W. Rodríguez; Jason Yang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Figure contents are not fully recoverable from the extracted text; the relevant tabulated results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares model size with downstream topic-quality metrics in a BERTopic pipeline, rather than measuring held-out pretraining cross-entropy or fitting language-model scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper tests whether embedding-model size affects topic coherence and diversity. Those are downstream topic-modeling outcomes relevant to V6. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss, tokens, training compute, extrapolation from small runs, or compute-optimal allocation. Cited scaling-law claims and descriptions of other topic-modeling work are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study varies embedding-model size (22M to 13B parameters) and reports downstream topic coherence and diversity in a BERTopic pipeline across 11 corpora. That is a new downstream setting bearing on V6. It measures no pretraining loss, fits, or allocation, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested. Size is confounded with model family, objective and training data: contrastive sentence-transformers, MLM encoders, and decoder-only LLaMA-2 used as an 8-bit embedder. So this is not a controlled scale ladder.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that encoder size (22M–13B) has negligible impact on BERTopic topic coherence and diversity, and that small models such as DistilBERT and MiniLM match larger ones. The quantization claim is not backed by any reported unquantized-vs-quantized comparison. Only quantized LLaMA results appear in the tables, despite the claim that each model was tested both ways.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares pretrained embedding models in a BERTopic topic-modeling pipeline and reports topic coherence and diversity, not held-out next-token cross-entropy or scaling-law fits.
record.method_sensitivity: Results are reported by dataset. BERTopic's default clustering parameters determine the number of topics, and the authors note that changing this setting could slightly alter the metrics. LLaMA-2 results are quantized; LLaMA-2 13B was not run unquantized because of hardware constraints.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are provided in Tables 4.1–4.2. The comparison uses BERTopic's default, potentially model-dependent number of topics; the authors acknowledge that changing this setting may alter scores. LLaMA-2 13B has no unquantized result, and several table entries were not evaluated. The evidence is topic quality in one pipeline, not general downstream capability or pretraining loss.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, coherence results for Amazon Reviews, CORD-19, IMDb, and Pushshift, and diversity results for Amazon Reviews, CORD-19, IMDb, PubMed, Pushshift, Reuters, Wikipedia, and Yahoo Answers were omitted. The omitted values are in Tables 4.1 and 4.2. Reuters and Yahoo Answers also have missing model entries as indicated in the tables.

untested.parts: No other modalities, repeated data, or fine-tuning or transfer power laws.
Untested: prediction from pretraining loss, and same-family scale ladders. Only BERTopic coherence (Cv) and diversity are measured, across heterogeneous off-the-shelf models.

missing.what: Mean topic coherence across datasets vs model size (log scale), with SD error bars. This is the paper's summary of the size trend; the values are not recoverable from the text.

record.verdict_notes: The per-row 'absent' states describe the group pattern, since no row has a stated baseline; MiniLM-L6 (22M) serves as the implicit baseline. BBC News coherence rises slightly from MiniLM-L6 (0.4932) to BERT-base (0.5194), but not monotonically with size. Reasons this is not labelled 'challenges': the LLaMA-2 models are not trained as sentence embedders, the c-TF-IDF/HDBSCAN stages may bottleneck quality, and the number of topics varies by model. Diversity sits near ceiling (~0.99) on most corpora. There is no uncertainty in the tables. The rows_left_out declaration covers the omitted datasets. The paper cites Kaplan et al. only as background.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law relationship with parameter count, tokens, or compute is measured.
No power-law fits or extrapolations from small runs are tested.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and tokens is tested.
The study does not hold parameter count fixed while varying depth, width, or architecture.
The experiments use text embedding models for topic modeling; other modalities, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, and transfer power laws are not tested.
Only topic coherence and topic diversity in this BERTopic setting are evaluated; other downstream tasks and prediction from pretraining loss are not tested.
The study does not fit or compare scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits, nor test how those fits depend on setup choices.

relationships.condition: BERTopic topic coherence and diversity using heterogeneous off-the-shelf embedding models (22M–13B, LLaMA-2 8-bit quantized), default HDBSCAN topic count
relationships.reason: Coherence and diversity are flat and non-monotone across three orders of magnitude of size; e.g. AG News coherence is 0.8488 at 22M vs 0.8374 at 13B. Size is confounded with family and objective, so this qualifies rather than refutes V6 (rows C20_*–CWik_*, D20_*–DBBC_*).
relationships.display_finding: Coherence and diversity varied non-monotonically across three orders of magnitude, with AG News coherence at 0.8488 for 22M versus 0.8374 for 13B, although family and objective also differed.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Compared embedding models on the five listed coherence datasets and three listed diversity datasets
reader_labels.reason: Across the reported scores, larger models do not show a consistent downstream topic-quality improvement; the authors describe model-size effects as negligible. Rows C20_ML6–CWik_L13 and D20_ML6–DBBC_L13.
